content.thinking:
I'm planning the dwarf's proportions and skeleton structure in one careful pass—short legs, chunky build, with the spine chain and shoulder/hip joint positions mapped out before writing the actual rig code.

For world coordinates I'm treating +X as the left side (s=1), naming joints with "L" suffix accordingly, and sticking to safe, simple API calls like joints, chains, sweeps, and basic parts rather than riskier tools, planning spheres and boxes for eyes and brows instead of decals. Now I'm laying out the spine chain points from hips through chest, deciding how many named segments the catmull path needs.

I'm working out the neck and head chain as a continuation of the spine, placing the head tip joint and head sphere center, then figuring the jaw joint position relative to the head. I'm sketching overall body proportions for a dwarf-sized character — hip height, leg segment lengths, torso span, neck, and head radius — to keep the total height realistic around 1.3-1.4m including a helmet.

Now I'm defining the leg chain with hip, knee, and ankle joints bent forward, checking reach distances fit within limb length, then setting up the sweep thickness for the leg geometry and starting the boot box dimensions at the ankle.

For arms, I'm thinking about shoulder placement and how to pose the dwarf holding a two-handed blunderbuss while still keeping a readable neutral rest pose rather than a stiff T-pose.

I'll settle on an A-pose with arms slightly out, letting the right hand grip the blunderbuss resting butt-down near the foot, canted forward-out for a natural "at rest" stance rather than actively aiming it.

I need the gun line to pass through the hand position, so I'm defining the butt and muzzle coordinates so the barrel runs diagonally from near the hip up through the gripped hand, keeping total length close to a blunderbuss's realistic size.

Then I'm checking the arm reach from shoulder to that hand point - the distance comes out very close to the combined upper and lower arm length, meaning the elbow stays nearly straight with just a slight bend angled back and outward.

For hands I'll keep it simple: a fist box at the chain tip with a few small finger capsules curled around it, generic enough to work for both gripping a weapon or hanging free, skipping individual digit joints since the wrist counts as the tip. Now thinking about shoulder pauldrons as larger armor pieces.

Writing geometry code...

For the tunic I'm thinking deep blue cloth with a hand-rolled paint function instead of toon shading—blending warm highlights at the top with cooler tones below based on surface normal, plus some grain noise for texture.

Now I'm working out color variations by mixing with white or dark purple to get lighter and darker shades, keeping within the flat color budget since paints don't count against it. For the breastplate, I'm sculpting it as a scaled ellipsoid positioned over the chest to sit naturally within the torso's proportions, like a steel-blue armor piece layered on top.

I'm adjusting the plate so it extends just slightly beyond the torso surface rather than engulfing it entirely, keeping the tunic visible at the belly and arms. I'm also considering adding a small decorative detail at the front center—maybe a cluster of gold rivets or a subtle ridge—to give the armor some visual interest without resorting to logos or emblems.

Now I'm positioning thin strap-like torus loops across the chest for crossing leather belts, then working out the hip belt geometry, figuring out how the torus rotation and scaling interact to flatten the ring properly around the hips to match the torso's radius at that height.

Buckle placed at the belt's front, then I'm figuring out the leg covering below it—considering a kilt-like skirt made from an open cylinder or lathe geometry extending from the belt downward, weighing whether an open-ended shape would leave a visible hollow gap at the rim that the belt could hide.

Now I'm defining the kilt as a solid lathe shape with a closed outline, giving it thickness and a deep red leather color with vertical stitch stripes, sized to cover the thighs. Moving on to the head, I'm scaling a sphere for the skull and positioning it above the neck, then working out the joint chain from neck base through to the head with named points for the skeleton.

I'm setting up the full skeletal chain, deciding the spine joints and parenting the neck chain off the chest top, then placing the head joint tip with an upward aim and sizing the skull sphere since this dwarf has essentially no neck. Now I'm adding a jaw joint parented to the head, aimed outward, and starting to shape a chin piece that will be mostly hidden by the beard.

Now I'm adding facial details: a dark interior for the mouth tucked under the moustache, a bulbous ruddy nose sticking out from the skull front, rosy cheek spheres on either side, and small white eye spheres with dark pupils positioned symmetrically.

For the hair, I'm going with a classic dwarf ginger palette -- warm orange-red "#d9731f" with darker "#8f3a12" shading and gold accent rings for braids. I'm planning the beard as a swept hierarchical mass using a curved path from the chin down toward the chest, tapering in radius as it descends.

Still shaping beard geometry... I'm also thinking through attaching the beard to the head bone for simplicity, then adding two side braids built from chains of small tilted spheres following curved paths to mimic plaited hair.

Still shaping beard geometry...

I'm defining the beard's taper so it narrows to a point at the tip, applying a hair-strand gradient texture, then sketching curved moustache tubes sweeping outward from the nose with a smooth curling path.

Now I'm placing hair tufts behind and below the helmet, then outlining a lathed steel dome shape for the helmet using a set of axis-to-edge profile points that curve down from the crown to a wider brim.

I'm checking the helmet's size against the skull sphere's radius at various heights to make sure it sits properly over the head without the proportions looking off, so I'm adjusting the head and helmet vertical positions and dimensions to keep the dwarf's total height in the right range.

Now I'm adding helmet details: a gold brim ring torus at the base, a nasal guard bar positioned between the eyes above the nose bulb, and planning a crest fin along the top.

Adding swept ivory horns from the sides of the helm, plus a ring of gold rivets around the brim, and confirming the eye color sits correctly under the brow before moving on to the ears.

Now I'm working out the hands and arms: a clenched fist sphere at the wrist with a steel gauntlet cuff, and a swept forearm-to-upper-arm chain with varying radii to taper the limb naturally. I'm also figuring out sleeve coverage, with cloth on the upper arm transitioning to bare skin partway down the forearm.

Adding bracer and cuff rods...

I need to figure out which joint the shoulders should parent off of — chestTop should be the tip joint of the spine chain, so I'll use the last joint in spine.joints as chestJ rather than relying on an uncertain "tip" property.

For the arm chain, I'm defining limb() with points and bend vectors wrapped in an array, then naming the chain joints shoulder/elbow/wrist per side, with the hand as the implicit tip since there are two spans plus three names. Sweeping the chain accepts a radius array fine, and the pauldron can attach rigidly to the shoulder joint itself so it moves naturally with the rigged arm.

Now I'm moving on to setting up the legs chain.

Adding more geometry details...

Working out stock geometry via extrusion axes...

Still working out stock outline coordinates...

Trying to place the hand at the grip point on the stock axis, but the computed position is too low relative to shoulder height for a believable reach, so the gun's resting position needs raising rather than sitting flush on the floor.

Instead I'm having the hand grip the barrel farther up at around 55-60% along its length, which lands at a plausible height, with the stock butt resting on the floor below it in a "grounded arms" pose.

Setting the wrist target slightly behind the barrel axis so the hand wraps naturally, checking the reach distance from shoulder stays within limit, and adding an elbow bend hint pointing outward and back. Now I'm defining the barrel as a tapering tube from the grip point out to a flared bell shape at the muzzle.

Still writing barrel geometry...

Now I'm adding the flintlock mechanism—a small plate and cock positioned on the stock side, offset slightly in X to give it thickness, facing outward on the side the shooter would see.

Positioning the trigger guard torus with a rough rotation, accepting slight tilt inaccuracy for simplicity, then placing it along the gun axis. Skipping the sling detail and adding a butt plate box oriented along the stock.

Working out stock extrusion direction and wood grain paint axis, then checking barrel end positions in the rest pose to make sure the gun placement at x -.4 doesn't clip through the arm or pauldron geometry.

I'm figuring out the gun attachment at the wrist and whether to add a powder horn or bandolier strap, considering a diagonal strap sweep path from the left shoulder across the chest that stays clear of the chest plate's bounding box.

Working out strap geometry manually instead—computing z-height along the ellipsoid at each point of the diagonal path, clamping to zero outside the surface bounds so the strap hugs the chest plate properly.

Settling on a flattened circular cross-section for the strap sweep, then planning cartridge pouches as small vertical brass cylinders with gold-capped tops spaced along the strap.

I'm checking where the beard overlaps the strap and charges — since the beard hangs down to about y .74 and juts forward to similar depth as the charges, several of the lower charges near the center will be hidden behind it, so I'll just place them along the full strap length and accept partial occlusion.

I also need side pouches on the waist belt and a curved powder horn on the left hip, sketched as a short bending path from the hip outward.

Thinking about the left hand too, maybe instead of a gun give it a mug of ale for a fun character detail — a small wooden cylinder with metal bands, a handle torus, and a foam sphere on top, positioned just in front of the gripping fist.

For skin tone I'm leaning toward a ruddy dwarf complexion, something like a warm reddish-brown with mottled shading for the cheeks to add texture and realism.

Now I'm settling on a color palette inspired by bold Blizzard-style armor sets: royal blue tunic, bluish steel, brown leathers, gold trim, fiery orange-red hair, and warm skin tones against off-white accents.

Writing the lighting shader function...

I should make lit() resolve a flexible color input first, then build the tunic with a subtle vertical grain pattern between two blues since the torso is mostly covered by plate armor anyway. For decoration I want to avoid anything resembling existing game logos, so I'll design a simple original tabard emblem instead.

I'm positioning a small hanging tabard box at the kilt's front with its own mountain-and-sun motif, sizing it to fit between the belt and the kilt's lower edge, and making sure the plane texture only faces forward.

Writing SVG tabard code...

Now I'm checking the plane decal's placement against the kilt's curved surface, making sure the pennant sits flush at the center and doesn't clip through the rounded profile as it extends outward.

The tabard extends lower than the kilt, hanging freely in front of the knees without clipping since it's positioned in front of the legs. I'll attach it to the belt independently. For the back, I'm adding a bedroll cylinder plus straps, a leather backpack box with a flap, and a canteen to round out the gear.

Now I'm adding small details: a hung bronze mug, white eye spheres, and finger geometry for the hands—building a fist shape around the barrel grip with knuckle capsule rods positioned along the hand to make the grip look natural.

Then I'm mirroring this for the left fist with curled finger capsules, plus small flourishes like elbow rivets and sleeve cuffs, and working on eye details with blue irises, pupils, and angled bushy brow boxes for each side of the face.

Still placing belt studs and eye geometry...

Now I'm working out the jaw structure as a scaled sphere positioned below the skull with its own bone and joint aimed downward, letting the beard cover most of it while the head stays attached properly. I'm also figuring out where to tuck a small dark mouth shape into the jaw seam, mostly hidden beneath the moustache.

Next I'm thinking through the shoulder pauldron geometry—a hemisphere shell scaled and positioned on the shoulder bone, then working out the rotation math so it tilts outward correctly depending on which side (left or right) it's on.

Still writing pauldron geometry...

I'm defining a lathe outline for the dome shape with height-based coloring so the rim paints gold while the body stays steel, then stacking three scaled pauldron lathes and applying the same lathe approach to the helmet.

Checking total height — about 1.43m is a bit tall for a dwarf, so I'm adjusting the head position lower, around HY=1.12, and reworking the neck chain path to fit the shorter proportions.

Now I'm shaping the beard, defining its path from the jaw down to belt level around y=.67, and tapering its width and depth with radius functions that shrink as it goes down.

Setting facial feature positions relative to head center, then placing sideburn sweeps connecting helmet to beard and starting a hair sweep flowing behind the helmet...

Shortening the hair mane to avoid intersecting shoulders and backpack, then defining the full color palette: skin tones, hair colors, steel and gold shades for the armor and accents.

Now I'm setting up the file imports for the TypeScript build, pulling in Three.js, the builder, and IK limb functions, trimming unused imports to avoid typecheck errors.

Writing meta and imports...

Adding ground darkening and dirt blending for boots, then starting to define the paint palette...

Now I'm building the hips joint as root and setting up the spine chain with a catmull-rom curve through the torso.

Working out the radius curve for the torso sweep...

Now I'm placing a sphere plate on the chest, checking that its scale and offset keep it slightly in front while staying flush with the torso's back profile at that height.

Adding a darker steel back plate positioned slightly inward, then planning gold trim details — a curved ridge line following the ellipsoid's front surface, plus gold rivet spheres positioned symmetrically on the chest. I'm also starting to design a gorget-style collar ring at the neck.

Now I'm moving to the leg construction, setting hip and foot joint positions and building a chained limb structure for each side with named joints and contact points, while working out how the bend parameter should be shaped—whether as a single direction vector or a list of them.

Writing leg parts code...

Still shaping boot geometry...

Adding a cuff ring and buckle box, then a steel kneecap piece with a gold rivet attached to the knee joint bone. I'm skipping the thigh tasset but considering a pants stripe texture, then moving to describe the arm parts before writing a tabard SVG with a pennant-shaped path.

Still writing SVG code...

I verify the direction vector is normalized, then set up a basis point and helper function to compute positions along two axes for extruding the gun stock geometry, with wood coloring and bevel applied to the wrist bone. Still writing stock extrusion...

Now I'm defining the barrel as a swept shape between two points with a radius function and flat caps, then adding gold bands at intervals along the barrel by computing positions and radii along a normalized parameter and placing short rod segments at each one.

Next I work out the muzzle: a torus lip at the barrel's end, a dark interior disc set slightly forward to suggest depth into the bore, and a breech sphere where the barrel meets the stock to visually bridge the two pieces.

Now I'm positioning the lock plate on the side of the stock near the breech, a thin brass box oriented with its narrow dimension facing outward, plus a small cocked-hammer box angled off to the side.

For the trigger guard, I'm placing a torus ring beneath the grip in the gap region of the outline, making sure its center sits beyond the stock's bottom edge so it doesn't intersect the wooden body rather than cutting through the stock's center plane.

Then I'm skipping the sling detail and adding a thin wooden ramrod running along the barrel's underside, plus small gold inlay spheres along the stock's outer side face for decorative engraving.

Now I'm assembling the backpack: a leather box body, straps, a horizontal bedroll cylinder with striped end caps, and a small hanging gray cooking pot, all positioned relative to the character's torso and bone joints.

I'm figuring out torus rotation for the belt — rotating 90° about x turns the flat ring vertical so it wraps around the hips correctly, with a scale adjustment on the y-axis to give it depth after rotation. Then I'm placing evenly spaced belt studs around the loop using a sine/cosine angle calculation.

Now I'm working out the gold buckle placement centered on the belt front, plus the torso's taper curve using a power function along its height.

Working through belt dimensions now: setting ring radius .235 with tube .035, placing studs and buckle box relative to that, then starting to shape the kilt outline so its top sits just under the belt.

Still thinking through kilt profile geometry...

For the kilt I want a proper tartan plaid pattern rather than solid color, so I'm working out a paint function based on the lathe's height and angle coordinates to create crossing stripes.

Confirming the paint resolution correctly threads `current` through nested calls. Now I'm defining the torso tunic color, sleeve bands with skin/tunic paint fills, eye colors, and setting up the rig's neck-to-head joint chain.

I realize chain tips don't automatically inherit a "head" role, so I'll simplify by building a short neck chain with a single joint and then attaching a separate head joint with its own role and aim direction.

Adding the jaw joint off the head, skipping tail and finger digits for simplicity, and now sketching the fist geometry for the right hand using a scaled sphere.

Still writing hand code...

Working out the mug handle geometry: the ring sits where it overlaps the mug body edge, and the fist sphere is sized to reach and overlap the ring, so visually it reads as a fist gripping the handle with fingers passing through the opening.

For the mug itself, I'm setting up a wood cylinder body with gold torus bands, a foam sphere top, and ring details. Then I'm placing a powder horn on the left hip using a curved sweep path with tapering radius, brass cap and ivory ends, positioned away from the gun side near the leg and thigh bones.

Checking the hand position relative to the horn confirms no overlap, so now I'm calculating belt pouch placement against the kilt's curved surface — figuring out the outer radius at the pouch's height and x-position to get the correct z-depth, then adding a slight yaw rotation and a thinner leather flap on top.

Mirroring the pouch to the left side symmetrically, then working out the diagonal strap path across the chest using the plate's curvature formula to determine z-depth at each point along the strap.

I'll use the same radius function as the sweep, but simplify the strap cross-section to a plain circle rather than a flattened ellipse since the normal-aligned radii are unpredictable, and add a gold buckle sphere at the strap midpoint. For the cartridges, I'm checking visibility against the beard width at each shoulder position and spacing them along u from .02 to .18 in .06 steps so they peek out just beside the beard.

I'm placing six cylindrical brass cartridge charges with leather caps hanging along the strap, offset slightly outward and down from the strap centerline. Now I'm adding gold studs to the pauldrons, skin-toned arms with an elbow rivet, and a left elbow bracer, then double-checking the TypeScript types for part geometry, rotation, scale, and position arrays before writing the final code.

Writing braid loop code...

Still writing braid knots and gold ring details...

Still shaping the moustache curve, then adding eyebrow boxes positioned just above eye height using the darker hair color, bound to the head bone for both sides.

I'm working out the eyebrow rotation so they angle inward and downward for an angry expression, flipping the sign of the z-rotation between the left and right side so the inner ends slope toward center.

Now I'm checking whether the helmet brim covers the brows and eyes properly, adjusting the brim height and radius so the eyes stay visible underneath while the brows are mostly tucked under the rim, and raising the helmet base so it clears the top of the skull.

Nose bulb placement checks out with the guard ending above it. Now I'm adding cheek guard plates as angled boxes hanging from the sides of the helm near the ears, and setting up a gold band painted along the lathe profile using a height-based coordinate check.

Still writing paint logic... Then I'm placing ten rivets evenly around the brim circle using sine and cosine for their positions, and defining the crest as an extruded outline shape mounted above the helm's crown.

Working out the vertical stacking: helm base sits at HY+.09, rises .205 to its top near 1.415, and the crest embeds slightly into the dome from 1.33 up to about 1.445. I'm extruding the crest outline along the x-axis with a thin .03 depth and coloring it red for a plume effect, which reads as a cool accent piece. Now I'm sketching the horn geometry as a catmull-rom sweep curving outward from the helm's sides.

For the horns, I'm tapering the radius from .03 down to a point, giving them an ivory bone-like finish with flat caps, but I notice the curve pushes the tip too high past 1.48, so I'm rescaling the control points to bring the top down to about 1.39. Checking total height against the "1-1.4m" target, I'm nudging the crest base and top down slightly to land around 1.42, deciding that's close enough rather than re-tuning the base neck height. I estimate the full model will land around 230 parts, and I'm skipping any glowing rune on the chest or gun to avoid pulling in extra imports. Now I'm starting to write the actual file, being careful with TypeScript loop syntax over the left/right sides and figuring out the elbow bend direction hints for each arm.

Writing limb and pauldron code...

Still writing spike placement...

Checking the pauldron rim position against the shoulder arm sweep radius versus dome radius—looks consistent. Now I'm considering whether the neck needs a tunic collar.

Positioning ears as skin-toned spheres near the head, partly hidden by cheek guards, and adding rosy cheek and nose spheres for facial detail. I'm debating whether to add a mouth under the moustache, then placing a jaw sphere and checking that the skull sphere already covers that lower region.

Adjusting the skull and jaw sphere positions and scales so they fit together without redundancy, deciding to skip extra stubble or beard cards and skip a ground plinth. I'm ready to write out the final file carefully, double-checking for any unused imports before finalizing.

Checking which imports are actually used—mottle for skin, grain for fabrics, noise, resolve, mix, smoothstep, paint, catmull, svg, limb, OutlinePoint, ColorInput, lerp, and THREE—then starting to define the palette object with lit/mottle/grain calls for skin, tunic, pants, and leather materials.

Still defining materials...

Now I'm planning hair and beard shading with nested grain layers for highlight streaks, confirming the mottle signature matches string color inputs, and thinking through how the plaid kilt and pants paint apply to the legs versus where the kilt covers the hips.

For the pelvis, I'm positioning a partial sphere scaled to form pants at the hip, checking whether it's hidden by the torso's bottom cap before finalizing the full code.
